accepted.trend: Bengaluru offices are short of desks after shrinking their footprint during the work-from-home years, now that staff are mandated back five days a week.
accepted.context: Urban Indian tech workers forced back to physical offices to justify commercial leases, only to face lack of infrastructure.
accepted.angle: You fought the management to save your commute, but you have to fight your own colleagues just to get a physical chair.
slides: Your company spent six months mandating five days in office.

"Yaar, empty desk dikhna toh batana."
"Meeting room block kar le, wahan se kaam karenge."
"Cafeteria mein charging point chal raha hai?"
"Main washroom ja raha hoon, seat rakhna please."

You spent two hours in traffic.

To work from a beanbag.
accepted.caption: The collaboration has been extremely high dynamic. 💻

accepted.trend: Bengaluru offices are short of desks after shrinking their footprint during the work-from-home years, now that staff are mandated back five days a week.
accepted.context: Corporate employees being forced into gamified systems just to perform basic administrative tasks like sitting down.
accepted.angle: The office is no longer a workplace; it is a live multiplayer battle royale for basic office supplies.
slides: There is an app on your phone that decides if you are allowed to sit.

The company has 14,000 employees.
The company has 8,000 desks.
You must book Seat 42B three days in advance.

If you are late, your colleague takes your monitor.

Welcome back to the culture.
accepted.caption: Highly collaborative environment. 🤝

accepted.trend: Furniture and appliance rental plans from around Rs 2,699/month are growing across Indian metros against Rs 3-4 lakh setup costs.
accepted.context: Urban migrants in their late 20s and early 30s who move frequently and cannot afford or justify buying permanent furniture.
accepted.angle: Our parents built permanent lives with heavy steel; we rent a temporary existence that can be repossessed if our card declines.
slides: Compare your assets with what your father owned at your age.

At 30, your father bought a Godrej steel almirah.
It survived three house shifts.
It survived two city moves.
It is currently holding your original degree certificate.

You pay ₹2,699 a month for a bed.

If you miss the subscription, they take your sleep.
accepted.caption: The modern asset-light lifestyle. 🛏️

accepted.trend: Furniture and appliance rental plans from around Rs 2,699/month are growing across Indian metros against Rs 3-4 lakh setup costs.
accepted.context: The illusion of independent adult life in metros where every physical item is actually on loan.
accepted.angle: You are living in a display flat where even your comfort is a recurring liability.
slides: The itemised monthly invoice of your independence.

Rented 2-BHK flat: ₹35,000
Rented double bed: ₹1,200
Rented smart TV: ₹899
Rented washing machine: ₹600

"When are you settling down?"

When the subscription expires.
accepted.caption: Everything is temporary except the recurring bills. 💸
